newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swisscargo, Sabena boost German mkt share.
newsitem.headline: Swisscargo, Sabena boost German mkt share.

text.p: Swisscargo, the cargo arm of Swissair, said it is winning market share in Germany thanks to the additional freight capacity of Sabena.

The airline's general cargo manager Germany, Ulf Steinmann, told Reuters in an interview that 25 percent more freight capacity and access to Sabena's Brussels hub should boost Swissair cargo sales strongly this year.
Swisscargo took over global sales and marketing of Sabena's freight on January 1 this year as part of the Swiss airline's operational takeover of the Belgian carrier.
"We are showing an increase in freight which is certainly due to the Sabena capacity but we cannot yet analyse the traffic flows," he said.
"But we have clearly been able to increase our market share," he added.
Steinmann said the main advantages in Germany from the Sabena freight takeover were a capacity rise of 25 percent and the chance to sell destinations through a second hub.
"From Germany I can serve both hubs, Brussels as much as Zurich," he pointed out.
All freight capacity on Sabena flights was now sold on Swissair air waybills with a single set of rates for freight flown on both airlines.

Swissair could now also offer a more reliable European product using Sabena out of Brussels since the flexible Swissair use of Airbuses out of Zurich had often meant short-notice changes for freight, Steinmann noted.

"Together with this new capacity we have made our European rates more simple. We are now offering from all German airports the same rates to destinations whereas before we had different rates from different airports," he said.
Since March 1, Swissair was thus routeing European airfreight via Brussels to use the quick turnaround times at the Belgian airport, he explained.
Overall, Swisscargo aimed for a 25 percent productivity increase this year to match the 25 percent additional cargo capacity, he added.
"The integration of Sabena (freight) has gone very positively for us despite its speed. Clients have accepted Swissair as the sales and marketing partner for Sabena," he added.
Steinmann said he planned to carry 25,000 tonnes of German freight this year compared to 21,000 tonnes in 1996.
About 80 percent of this is trucked to Zurich or Brussels for onward air transportation, he noted.
